title: Russia to use tobacco sales licensing fees to fund healthcare
summary: Russia’s State Duma passed amendments to the budget code in their third reading that direct revenue from tobacco licensing fees toward regional healthcare funding, among other provisions. The Russian government proposed the amendments. Since October 1, Russia has charged a state fee for licenses to sell tobacco and nicotine-containing products at wholesale and retail.

title: Kazakhstan wanted to transfer Chechen activist Mansur Movlaev to Russia in secret. He twice attempted suicide, fearing extradition.
summary: On November 24, Kazakh authorities tried to transfer Chechen activist Mansur Movlaev from a pretrial detention center in Almaty to Petropavl without notifying his lawyers. The planned transfer came to light by chance. The detention center refused to accept a package for Movlaev because the paperwork showed he had already left for Petropavl, where prisoners are handed over to Russian authorities.

title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
summary: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

title: Frecce Tricolori’s New M-346 Seen During Rehearsal Ahead of Official Unveiling
summary: The new M-346 for the Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team was flown by a Leonardo test pilot during a rehearsal ahead of its official presentation later this week. Frecce Tricolori’s new M-346 jet is preparing for its official unveiling later this week, with a Leonardo test pilot rehearsing a flight demo on Nov. 23, 2026, over the company’s facilities in Venegono.

title: Watch: Moment troops raid home and capture Mexican drug lord
summary: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.

title: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering
summary: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering.

title: Russian lawmakers approve tighter monitoring of bank transfers between individuals to uncover untaxed income
summary: Russia’s State Duma has passed a law tightening oversight of bank transfers between individuals. Russia’s central bank and the Federal Tax Service (FTS) will monitor these transfers. The central bank will analyze transactions in individuals’ bank accounts and notify the Federal Tax Service if it detects signs of “systematic receipt of income from other individuals.”

title: Minister ponders stricter regime for migrant workers, and energy issues
summary: Latvia's new Minister of Economics Edgars Štelmahers (United List) plans to insist that the attraction of low-skilled labour to Latvia is more strictly regulated than hitherto, he told the Latvian Radio programme "Krustpunktā" (At the crossroads) on November 23rd.

title: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
summary: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.
